metadata.scoring_model: Cory Stout calibrated taste (not generic quality)

questions.question: What's a hill you'll die on that none of your friends agree with?
questions.justification: Forces self-examination, reveals identity, has social stakes via friend disagreement.

questions.question: What's the hardest phone call you've ever had to make?
questions.justification: Never asked. Concrete noun (phone call). Agency (had to make). Invites a deeply personal story.

questions.question: If your daily routine was a restaurant menu, what would the chef's special be?
questions.justification: Clever but passive observation. No stakes. Doesn't touch identity or agency.

questions.question: How many times have you moved in your life, and which move changed you the most?
questions.justification: Second part has depth but first part is database-recall. Borderline cavernous.

questions.question: What's the oldest thing in your closet that you refuse to throw away?
questions.justification: Concrete noun. Reveals identity through attachment. 'Refuse' implies agency/defense.

questions.question: Would you rather know the exact date of your death or never know?
questions.justification: Classic thought experiment asked a million times. No surprise factor.

questions.question: If you could put one sentence on every bathroom mirror in America, what would it say?
questions.justification: Concrete setting, reveals values, but slightly generic world-builder. Needs a twist.

questions.question: What's a version of yourself from 10 years ago that would be shocked by who you are now?
questions.justification: Self-examination, touches identity change, multi-layered — what shocks them could be good or bad.

questions.question: If you had to teach a one-hour class tomorrow on any topic with no prep, what would you teach?
questions.justification: Similar to the 8-scoring mandatory class but less stakes. 'No prep' adds pressure but 'any topic' is too open.

questions.question: What's something you quit that you still think about?
questions.justification: Never asked. Agency (they quit). 'Still think about' implies unresolved stakes. Haunting.

questions.question: Describing it like a heist movie, how did you get your current job?
questions.justification: Fun reframe but the metaphor might force too much. Slightly try-hard.

questions.question: Are you the person who leaves the party early or the one who turns off the lights?
questions.justification: Good identity sort, concrete, but slightly binary without depth. Missing a third option.

questions.question: How many books are within arm's reach of where you sleep?
questions.justification: Good specificity trap, reveals priorities, but might dead-end without conversation fuel beyond the number.

questions.question: What would your ex say is the most annoying thing about you?
questions.justification: Forces self-examination from specific person's perspective. Vulnerability. Multi-layered.

questions.question: What's your go-to karaoke song? Now: could you sing it right now, no music, and commit?
questions.justification: Fun escalation but more performance than revelation. Doesn't touch identity deeply.

questions.question: Would you rather be the best player on a losing team or the worst player on a championship team?
questions.justification: Good tension, reveals values, but asked before in various forms. Lacks surprise.

questions.question: What's a promise you made to yourself that you actually kept?
questions.justification: Agency. 'Actually kept' implies most people break self-promises — tension. Touches identity.

questions.question: If you had to open a shop on your block, what would you sell?
questions.justification: Good world-builder, concrete, but more whimsical than revealing.

questions.question: What's a piece of advice you ignored that turned out to be right?
questions.justification: Story-inviting. Self-examination. Stakes (they were wrong). Concrete.

questions.question: What's the last thing you did for the first time? When was it?
questions.justification: Time machine + agency. Reveals how adventurous/stagnant someone is. 'When' adds a second punch.

questions.question: If every lie you've ever told turned your skin slightly blue, how blue would you be right now?
questions.justification: Fun but answer is just a shade of blue. Not much conversation fuel without follow-up.

questions.question: If your bank account was a Yelp review, what would the one-star complaint be?
questions.justification: Clever reframe but financial questions make people defensive. Stakes aren't personal enough.

questions.question: Do you fight for things or let things find you?
questions.justification: Touches agency directly. Multi-layered — different answers for different domains. Simple to answer, deep to debate.

questions.question: What's the last thing you made that didn't work?
questions.justification: Good vulnerability but 'made' is slightly vague. Close to 9-scoring 'built with hands' but inverted.

questions.question: To the best of your ability, explain why you chose the city you live in — like you're defending it in court.
questions.justification: Explain-it test + reframe. 'Defending in court' adds stakes. Reveals values through location choice.

questions.question: What's the last fight you had that you're glad you had?
questions.justification: Agency (fought). Surprise (glad about a fight). Invites a STORY. Multi-layered — what made it worth it?

questions.question: What's a belief you held at 20 that you've completely abandoned?
questions.justification: Self-examination. Time anchor (20). 'Completely abandoned' has conviction. Reveals growth.

questions.question: When's the last time you apologized and actually meant every word?
questions.justification: Agency. 'Actually meant every word' implies most apologies are partial — tension.

questions.question: What's the last compliment someone gave you that you didn't believe?
questions.justification: Vulnerability. The gap between how others see you and how you see yourself. Surprising angle.

questions.question: What's one thing you do that your parents never did?
questions.justification: Generational break. Agency. Touches the moment someone chose their own path. Never asked.

questions.question: What's the last risk you took that your friends thought was stupid?
questions.justification: Agency. Social stakes. Story-inviting. Friend judgment adds concrete tension.

questions.question: If you could go back and watch yourself handle one specific conversation, which one?
questions.justification: Implies regret or pride. Specific (one conversation). Self-examination.

questions.question: What's the most important thing in your life that you never talk about at dinner parties?
questions.justification: Hidden self. Public/private contrast. Asks what's never discussed. Real weight.

questions.question: Are you building something right now or recovering from something?
questions.justification: Deep self-sorting. Both answers reveal current life chapter. Simple to answer, deep to unpack.

questions.question: What's a skill you taught yourself that nobody knows you have?
questions.justification: Agency (taught yourself). Secret identity element. Concrete. Never asked at parties.

questions.question: What rule do you break on purpose and feel fine about?
questions.justification: Mirror of 9-scoring 'rule nobody taught you.' Agency. Reveals values through transgression.

questions.question: If you had to live in one room for a year, what three objects are in it?
questions.justification: Good world-builder but constraint feels too artificial. Desert island variant.

questions.question: What do your hands look like right now? What do they say about your week?
questions.justification: Beautifully concrete but might dead-end. First part is observation, not agency.

questions.question: What's something you used to judge people for that you now do yourself?
questions.justification: Self-examination at its finest. Hypocrisy as self-knowledge. Vulnerability + growth.

questions.question: How many people have you cut out of your life on purpose?
questions.justification: Specificity trap with real stakes. Number IS the personality reveal. 'On purpose' = agency.

questions.question: What's the last thing you started over from scratch?
questions.justification: Agency. Implies failure and courage. Story-inviting. 'From scratch' is concrete.

questions.question: If your inner monologue was broadcast to everyone in this room for 10 seconds, what would they hear?
questions.justification: Fun but answer is too performative — people will pick something witty rather than honest.

questions.question: What's the most expensive lesson you've learned for free?
questions.justification: Great reframe. Implies pain without asking for it. 'Expensive + free' = tension. Multi-layered.

questions.question: Are you the same person when nobody's watching?
questions.justification: Touches identity but too philosophical — feels like a fortune cookie. Needs more specificity.

questions.question: Would you rather be deeply understood by one person or widely admired by thousands?
questions.justification: Good binary but asked before. 'Right' answer is too obvious. Lacks surprise.

questions.question: What's something you rebuilt after it broke?
questions.justification: Agency. Could be literal or metaphorical. Story-inviting. Rebuilding implies loss + determination.

questions.question: What's the last thing you Googled? Now — what were you actually looking for?
questions.justification: Chain that deepens. Second question is the real one — separates surface from need. Surprising.

questions.question: If your apartment burned down tonight, what would you realize you didn't need?
questions.justification: Inversion of classic 'what would you save.' Reveals attachment patterns.

questions.question: If you had to write one sentence that your kid reads on their 18th birthday, what would it say?
questions.justification: Emotional but too Hallmark. 'One sentence' format done before. Invites performance over honesty.

questions.question: What's the last promise you broke to yourself?
questions.justification: Agency. Vulnerability. Self-examination. 'Last' anchors it. Companion to 'promise you kept.'

questions.question: What's something you're proud of that you'd never put on a resume?
questions.justification: Hidden self. Agency (proud of). Concrete anchor (resume). Inversion of social performance.

questions.question: What's a part of your personality that only shows up under pressure?
questions.justification: Self-examination. Hidden self. Implies self-knowledge under stress. Specific.

questions.question: What did you stop pretending to enjoy, and when?
questions.justification: Agency (stopped pretending). Two temporal anchors. 'When' demands a specific story.

questions.question: What's the most valuable thing you own that you couldn't sell?
questions.justification: Reframe of value. Concrete noun. Tension between monetary and personal value.

questions.question: What's something that went completely wrong that you'd do again?
questions.justification: Inversion. Agency. Multi-layered — why do it again? Reveals values through failure.

questions.question: What would your 15-year-old self be disappointed about? What would they be amazed by?
questions.justification: Two temporal anchors. Dual question reveals different things. Concrete age.

questions.question: What's something you chose that nobody in your family would have chosen?
questions.justification: Agency. Generational break. 'Nobody' = never-asked territory. Identity through contrast.

questions.question: Is the version of you at work the real you, or the version of you at 2 AM?
questions.justification: Clever binary with good anchors but feels slightly try-hard. Too neat.

questions.question: What's a scar you're glad you have?
questions.justification: Inversion (glad about a scar). Concrete noun. Literal or metaphorical. Beautiful.

questions.question: How many of your current friendships would survive if you moved to another country tomorrow?
questions.justification: Specificity trap with real stakes. Number reveals depth of connections. 'Tomorrow' adds urgency.

questions.question: What's the best thing that happened to you because you were in the wrong place?
questions.justification: Inversion. Agency implied. Story-inviting. Surprise element.

questions.question: When did you first realize you were different from your parents?
questions.justification: Generational. Specific temporal anchor ('first realize'). Coming-of-age story. Agency.

questions.question: What's something you keep choosing even though it's harder?
questions.justification: Repeated agency. Implies easier path exists. Reveals values through sacrifice.

questions.question: What's something you believed last year that embarrasses you now?
questions.justification: Temporal change. Self-examination. 'Last year' is close enough to sting.

questions.question: What's the last thing you did that scared you? Would you do it again? Right now?
questions.justification: Three-beat chain with escalation. Agency. 'Right now' third beat adds present-tense pressure.

questions.question: If you had one year with no obligations and no money worries, what would you build?
questions.justification: 'Build' verb is strong but 'no money worries' removes too much real-world tension.

questions.question: What's the loneliest decision you've ever made?
questions.justification: 'Loneliest' before 'decision' is surprising. Agency. Vulnerability. Never asked. Multi-layered.

questions.question: What does your browser history say about you that your Instagram doesn't?
questions.justification: Clever contrast but similar energy to screen-time-billboard (scored 3). Too techy.

questions.question: Are you living the life you chose or the life that chose you?
questions.justification: Touches agency directly but too abstract. Feels like a bumper sticker.

questions.question: If everyone you've ever wronged was in the next room, who would you talk to first?
questions.justification: Real stakes. Forces prioritization of wrongs. Specific (one person). Vulnerability.

questions.question: What's something nobody asked you about that you wish they had?
questions.justification: Literally asks what's never asked. Hidden self. Meta-question that opens any door.

questions.question: What's the hardest thing you do that looks easy from the outside?
questions.justification: Hidden self. Inversion. Agency. Reveals effort behind the surface.

questions.question: Would you rather know what everyone thinks of you or never know?
questions.justification: Classic binary, asked many times. No surprise.

questions.question: What's a tradition you started for yourself?
questions.justification: Agency (started). Identity. Concrete. Reveals what they value enough to ritualize.

questions.question: What's the last thing you said no to that you wanted to say yes to?
questions.justification: Agency. Tension between desire and discipline. 'Last' anchors it. Story-inviting.

questions.question: What's the quietest rebellion you've ever staged?
questions.justification: Unexpected adjective + noun. Agency. Hidden self. 'Rebellion' = agency, 'quietest' = nobody saw.

questions.question: What's a ritual you do before something important that nobody knows about?
questions.justification: Self-imposed structure. Hidden self. Concrete ('before something important'). Agency.

questions.question: What's the strangest thing you've ever been grateful for?
questions.justification: Unexpected adjective + gratitude. Inversion. Slightly less story-inviting than top 9s.

questions.question: What would your best friend say you're in denial about?
questions.justification: Specific person (best friend). Stakes (denial). Uncomfortable self-examination.

questions.question: What's a line you drew for yourself that you've never crossed?
questions.justification: Self-imposed rule. 'Never crossed' implies temptation. Identity through restraint.

questions.question: What's the last thing you forgave yourself for?
questions.justification: Inversion (self-forgiveness, not forgiving others). Agency. Temporal anchor. Rarely asked.

questions.question: When's the last time you completely changed your mind in real time — mid-conversation?
questions.justification: Specific setting (conversation). Agency. Implies intellectual honesty. 'In real time' is concrete.

questions.question: What's the most important conversation you've ever had in a car?
questions.justification: Unexpected setting (car). Concrete noun. Universally relatable. Intimacy, movement, transition.

questions.question: What's something you do every day that you chose — not inherited, not required?
questions.justification: Self-imposed structure. Agency. 'Not inherited, not required' sharpens the question.

questions.question: What's a failure you've never told anyone about?
questions.justification: Hidden self. Vulnerability. 'Never told anyone' is powerful but might be TOO vulnerable for a bar.

questions.question: What would your mother say is your best quality that you don't see in yourself?
questions.justification: Specific person (mother). Inversion (quality you DON'T see). Emotional depth. Multi-layered.

questions.question: Are you more afraid of being forgotten or being misremembered?
questions.justification: Both options are scary. No 'right' answer. Touches legacy and identity. Surprise.

questions.question: What's the bravest thing you've done that nobody saw?
questions.justification: Unexpected adjective pairing. Hidden self. Agency. Inversion (unwitnessed bravery). Story-inviting.

questions.question: What's the smallest thing that completely changed your trajectory?
questions.justification: Inversion (small cause → big effect). Story-inviting. Reveals how they think about fate vs. agency.

questions.question: What's a version of success you used to want that would horrify you now?
questions.justification: Two temporal anchors. Inversion (wanted → horrified). Reveals growth through rejection. Never asked.

questions.question: What's something you used to do every day that you silently miss?
questions.justification: Temporal change. 'Silently' implies hidden self. Vulnerability. 'Every day' is concrete.

questions.question: What's the last door you walked through that you couldn't walk back through?
questions.justification: Metaphor works literally and figuratively. Irreversible agency. Story-inviting. Poetic but concrete.

questions.question: Who's the last stranger that changed your day? What did they do? Did you tell them?
questions.justification: Three-beat chain. Concrete. Third beat is the knife twist — implies most people don't acknowledge kindness.

questions.question: How many people in your life have ever seen you completely fall apart?
questions.justification: Specificity trap with vulnerability stakes. Number IS the personality reveal. 'Completely fall apart' has weight.

questions.question: What's something you protect that most people don't even think about?
questions.justification: Hidden self. Agency (protect). Slightly abstract — needs the answerer to make it concrete.

questions.question: When did you first feel like an adult — not by age, but by decision?
questions.justification: Reframe of common question. 'By decision' forces agency. Coming-of-age story. The parenthetical removes the boring answer.

questions.question: What's the most dangerous thing you do that's completely legal?
questions.justification: Inversion (dangerous + legal). Fun. Reveals risk tolerance. Concrete. Sparks debate.

questions.question: What's a goodbye you weren't ready for?
questions.justification: Vulnerability. Story-inviting. Concrete (a specific goodbye). Elegant simplicity.

questions.question: If you had to carve one sentence into the wall of your childhood bedroom, what would it say?
questions.justification: Emotional. But 'one sentence' format done before within this set. Slightly derivative.

questions.question: What's the last thing you chose to do the hard way?
questions.justification: Agency ('chose' is explicit). 'The hard way' implies easier path existed. Reveals values through effort.
